utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Good morning, Madam Registrar. Could you kindly call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is the case number IT-05-88-T, the Prosecutor versus Vujadin Popovic et al.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, ma'am. For the record, accused Popovic and Beara are still missing due to indisposition. We understand that the waivers will reach us in the course of today. Do I have a confirmation of that and also formal waiver from you, Mr. Zivanovic, and you Mr. Meek?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, of course, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Meek?

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. For the record also I notice the absence of Mr. Krgovic, of Ms. Condon and Mr. Ostojic. Anyone else? I don't think so. Prosecution is Mr. McCloskey and Mr. Vanderpuye. And we are sitting pursuant to Rule 15 bis today. Judge Stole couldn't be with us. All right. Now, we have concerns about the practice that has been resorted to with some of the recent witnesses where both Prosecution and Defence have exceeded the time that was indicated to us prior to the testimony. We do understand that sometimes this can become necessary but there are limits, and these limits are easy for you to understand, one of which was handed to me yesterday by Mr. McCloskey himself that sometimes we end up with witnesses here, staying here, for an entire week without being called to testify. I think out of all the options that we have, the first thing is that we try to deal with this in the same spirit that we have approached the testimony from the beginning of this trial, that is expecting both sides, Prosecution and Defence, to exercise self-restraint and self-discipline without the need of us interfering. Please don't force our hands because if you do, then we will have to intervene. As regards this witness, we have given it a lot of thought and we suggest to you that you do your utmost, all of you, to finish with this witness today. Yes, Mr. Haynes. First of all, let me say good morning to the witness. Good morning, Mr. Dragutinovic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We are continuing with your testimony. Mr. Haynes will continue his cross-examination. Mr. Haynes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Dragutinovic.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: When you were giving evidence-in-chief, you told us a little bit about the formation of Tactical Group 1 and I'm going to ask you just a few questions about that this morning. It's right, isn't it, that the formation of that group was substantially the responsibility of your commander, Vinko Pandurevic?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And once he had been tasked with the responsibility of forming Tactical Group 1, he had to require Dragan Obrenovic to come back to command the brigade because Dragan Obrenovic had been on sick leave in June. That's right also, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: I entirely understand if you couldn't answer this question, but do you have any recollection of the precise date upon which Dragan Obrenovic came back to the brigade on duty?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't remember the exact date.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: In relation to Tactical Group 1, you yourself gave the order to march, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I wrote it and it was on the basis of that order that the march took place.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Now, I just want to explore with you a little bit, and I'm going to show you some documents to help your memory, the -- about the composition of Tactical Group 1 and I wonder whether we could start by having P106, at page 48, put into e-court, please. No, I'm sorry, P106. I don't need a page for that document. And if the witness's attention could be focused on point 2. Can you look at that and read it to yourself, Mr. Dragutinovic, and then confirm to me that the contribution that the Zvornik Brigade made to Tactical Group 1 was a strengthened light infantry brigade, sorry, battalion, a strengthened light infantry battalion?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Paragraph 2(A), the Zvornik Brigade has to form a unit, one light battalion strong. That's what we did.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And in terms of the precise number of men that that involved, I'm going to show you another document now, it's P384, and this is page 48. I think if you read through this page of the war diary, it will show you that on the 4th of July, 407 men left the Standard barracks. Can the page go down, please? The relevant section isn't -- there you are.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It is a document of the war diary. It says, indeed, 407 men. However, the number I know, and the difference is small, is 394. We had formed a unit of 394 men but the discrepancy is minor.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Dragutinovic. That's very helpful. And in fact that number of men is rather smaller than one light infantry brigade, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Light infantry battalion, not brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Sorry, my mistake again. Light infantry battalion but 394 men is rather smaller than a light infantry battalion?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Battalion, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: So --

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: In any event, the suggestion that the Zvornik Brigade contributed two battalions to Tactical Group 1 would be quite incorrect, wouldn't it?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. That is not true.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Now, I want to move on to a particular unit of the Zvornik Brigade, that's the Podrinje Detachment, which you described in your evidence the other day as a manoeuvres battalion; is that correct? Those are the same things?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And with the assistance of some other brigade records, I'd like to confirm with you the size of that particular unit, and I wonder whether we could look at P382, please. We need to go, I think, to the second page of this document. Now, if you look at the fourth entry down, does that show the numbers in July of 1995 of the manoeuvres battalion of the Zvornik Brigade?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That is the status of the manoeuvring battalion of 360-something people. That's all the men who were in that manoeuvre battalion but that's not just the combat component. It includes the logistics and all the other non-combat components. The tactical group however included only the combat component.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And would that number also include members of that battalion who were on sick leave or wounded?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is the total number of men in that manoeuvre detachment, and all those who were included in the battalion, including everybody, those on sick leave, those who were wounded. They were not written off. They are included in the number.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Now, I want to move on a little to ask you about the operations that that unit was involved in in June and July of 1995. It's right, isn't it, that the manoeuvres battalion or the Podrinje Detachment, or the Drina Wolves as they are sometimes known, were engaged in the region of the Sarajevo Romanija brigade in July of 1995?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. One part of that detachment was in the area of the Sarajevo theatre of war. So not all of the detachment was part of Tactical Group 1.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Thank you. And just to get some idea of how many of that detachment were involved in the Sarajevo Romanija Brigade region, can we have a look at P378 at page 70? If you look at the entry for 1400 hours, for the 16th of June of 1995, I think you'll see that that shows that 85 men and eight vehicles of the manoeuvres battalion departed for the region of the Sarajevo Romanija Brigade; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. You can see it here. Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And was one of the commanders of that unit a man called Pepic?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that was the commander of that company that was in the Sarajevo theatre of war.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And we can see a little of what happened to him if we look at P377, at page 101. Can that be placed into e-court? The time we are looking for is 1405 so the page needs to go down a little bit and I think that shows us from the duty officer's notebook that Pepic, the commander of that brigade, was wounded in the region of Trnovo on about the 6th of July; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, 394 men were contributed by the Zvornik Brigade to Tactical Group 1, but that still left substantial numbers of men and resources available to the brigade's area of defence, didn't it?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes, because this Tactical Group 1 included only one light infantry battalion size unit, a smaller part of the Zvornik Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, I want to move on now, please, to the movements of Tactical Group 1, between the 4th of July and the 10th, please, and to that end I'm going to ask that 7D64 be put into e-court. And when it's there, we'll manoeuvre it appropriately so that you can mark it for us. You might have to wait a little while, Mr. Dragutinovic. This is a map and they take a bit of time to come up. I think we need to go south a little, and a bit more. That's perfect. Now, on the first day of march, the unit left Standard. Did it move all as one unit on that day?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We divided the march into two segments. In the first segment, the armoured mechanised company went on the route of Bjelovac, Pribicevac, et cetera and then the axis --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness repeat that? He did that very fast, much too fast.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Dragutinovic, can you repeat the last part of your answer, please? You said, "We divided the march into two segments. In the first segment, the armoured mechanised company went on the route of Bjelovac, Pribicevac ..." Can you continue from there, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Zvornik, Bratunac, Bjelovac, Sase, Pribicevac.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And the second segment?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And the second one, that's the infantry part, went Zvornik, Bratunac, Bjelovac, Skelani, Zeleni Jadar.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: I'm going to ask that you be provided with some pens now so you can mark on this map where the units moved to. We know that you began in Zvornik and you're not going to be able to show us that because it's too far north on the map so perhaps you can take the route from Bratunac, please, firstly of the mechanised unit, and then secondly of the infantry unit, and perhaps you could be -- mark those in two different colours. So firstly could you mark on the map the route that was taken by the mechanised unit?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think we can even zoom in. It would allow him to do that better.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: By all means, let's have a look. Can we zoom in one more time and see whether we can keep all of the relevant portions on the map? Now, can we go up a little bit? Yes. That might just do. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Armoured mechanised company, Bratunac, Bjelovac, Sase, Pribicevac.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And before you move on to the infantry brigade, did the armoured mechanised units reach Pribicevac on the first day of march or did it take more than one day to get there?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It arrived the same day, in the afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Now, perhaps in blue you could mark the movement of the infantry unit.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks] We need to move the map to the right so that I can find Skelani. Skelani is not visible in this section.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Well, what we are going to have to do then is you're going to have to erase all the marks you've made and then we are going to have to move the map because we can't move it once you've marked it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: What I suggest something. We can ignore this map completely, bring up again -- forget about this. Bring up the same map once more, with -- bring up the same mark, same zoom, zooming level, but move it a little bit to the right. And then he can repeat the markings.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You can zoom out and I will mark.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You have to go up a little bit.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Just a little up. Perfect.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I draw that?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, go ahead, please, thank you, Mr. Dragutinovic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: That's very well drawn if I may say so. Would you put next to the red line, AU or AMU, armoured mechanised unit?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks] I need red.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And next to the blue line, can you put IU for infantry unit?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And would you at the finishing positions of those marches just perhaps put an X or a dot? One in red, one in blue, preferably?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Thank you. And those Xs represent the positions that each of those units had reached by, as it were, the end of the march on the 4th of July; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This red line depicts the movement of the armoured mechanised company on the same day and the blue line shows the total route covered by the infantry component that started on the 4th and arrived at the destination on the 5th. It spent the night in the area of Jezero, that I can mark.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: But I don't quite see --

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Well, if it's not on the map, mark the position to the best of your recollection where it would be on the map, please.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Have you marked it, Mr. Dragutinovic?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Oh, it's in the bottom right-hand corner, yes, thank you. And would you just put next to that X, 4/7 to indicate the 4th of July, the point at which the infantry unit stopped its march for the night?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, which of those units were you with?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The armoured mechanised company.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And which of those units was the commander with, Mr. Pandurevic?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Commander Pandurevic was with the other element, the infantry element that was moving along the Bratunac-Skelani-Zeleni Jadar route.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: During the days between the 4th and the 10th of July, did the armoured mechanised unit move from the position where you've marked the X?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Depending on the combat activities.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Was that a forward movement or movement to support combat activities and returning to Pribicevac which was a forward command post, as I understand it?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Movement forwards, in order to provide support to the units that were engaged in combat at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And what direction did the infantry unit move after the 4th of July?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: After the 4th of July, it moved towards the lake, Zeleni Jadar, and there it stayed until the 6th, the morning of the 6th.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And after the morning of the 6th, was it involved in combat activities with the forces of the 28th Division in the region of Zeleni Jadar?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. As early as on the 6th of July, in the morning, combat started, units joined the fight, and it lasted until the early evening.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Can you describe for us, please, the strength of the resistance of the forces of the 28th Division throughout the 6th, 7th and 8th of July?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: After the units joined the fight in the morning of the 6th, and after being engaged in combat until the evening, our forces did not carry out their task. They were unable to push back the units of the 28th Division along this axis that was assigned to us, so we ceased our attacks sometime in the evening.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And where did the infantry unit and in particular Commander Pandurevic spend the night of the 6th of July?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the sector of our command post, which was located at the Javor elevation. I can't find it probably because this is a smaller scale map but it should be somewhere here, between those two crosses that I marked here, that was on the 6th. This is where we established our command.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Now, were there combat activities on the 7th and could you briefly describe them to us?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: After the failure to carry out the task on the 6th, the commander brought together the commands of the combat groups 1 and 2 and decided to group them and to take another axis, Javor-Biljeg. And the start of the attack was scheduled for the morning of the 7th. But it was foggy. The weather was bad. It was raining. So we stopped our attack along this axis that I just mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And again, on the 7th of July, where did Commander Pandurevic spend the night?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the sector where the Javor elevation was, in the immediate vicinity of the units that were getting ready for the combat action. That would be Combat Group 1.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: Tactical Group 1.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Could we briefly move to the 8th of July and could you describe for us then the combat activities of Tactical Group 1?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When the fog dispersed and when the weather improved, that was in the afternoon, the units headed along the axis that was assigned to them, and after about an hour or two of fighting, they were able to capture the Biljeg feature and then they continued their attack and captured the heights that we called Tri Sise. That's what we called them. They did not have a name. So this was our immediate task, to do so. And after capturing those features, our next task was to reach the Zeleni Jadar-Srebrenica road, and our units were to prepare for the next day there.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Is this map sufficiently detailed for you to indicate where the three hills were that you captured on the 8th of July?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think the scale is too small. We should zoom in and then I would be able to see but I can see now that it's impossible to see the features that I need.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We can mark this one and save it, Mr. Haynes, and then zoom in on the area where you wish to direct the witness to. And he can mark that area.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Before he does, I wonder if he could just indicate the positions for the 6th of July and the 7th of July where, to his knowledge, Commander Pandurevic spent the night.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. By all means.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Should I mark?

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Yes, please, Mr. Dragutinovic.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I will mark it on this map here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's make things clear. What are you going to mark? I want to make sure that you have understood Mr. Haynes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Would you mark firstly a position between the two Xs with 6/7 to indicate the position where Commander Pandurevic spent the night of the 6th of July?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've already told you that this map is too small, the scale is too small.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Well, you appear to have marked it. And then if it's a position very different, 7/7, the position where approximately he spent the night of the 7th of July.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it was in the same place, so the 6th to the 7th and the 7th to the 8th, those two nights he spent at the same place.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Thank you. That's very helpful. Well, in that case, can you just sign this map in the bottom left-hand corner and date it the 15th of June 2007 and then we can call it up again and expand it a bit further?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks] 15th.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. We can save that, and I suggest we bring up the same map again and we zoom, as much as we can, the area south of Srebrenica. I think it can go one further. Yeah. Stop there. Does it help you, Mr. Haynes or not?

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Well, I'm really interested is whether the witness can identify on there where the three hills are and perhaps he could put 3T by the position.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Why 3T and not 3H?

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Because of the description he gave of them yesterday. But 3H in the interests of political correctness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Dragutinovic, have we zoomed too much or is it okay for you? Yeah, okay. He's identified them.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Perfect. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Thank you. And --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: While we are here, perhaps he could indicate again on this map if it is possible, the locations where your client supposedly slept on the 6th and on the 7th. It would be more precise than we had it on the previous map.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President, that's very helpful.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes. What mark should I put? Or should I just put in the date?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, the date 6/7 and 7/7.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Now, can we move to the 9th of July and can you describe to us, please, the combat activities of the unit on the 9th of July?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, since the units were able to reach the Srebrenica-Zeleni Jadar road, to the north of those three nameless hills and Biljeg, they continued with their actions in the area of the Zeleni Jadar-Srebrenica road, heading towards the village of Rajne and they launched an attack on the axis, Tri Sise hills-Zivkovo Brdo -- hill.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And on the 9th of July was there still strong resistance from the forces of the 28th Division?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And where on the 8th of July, again if it can be marked on the map, did the units and Commander Pandurevic spent the night?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can mark it here. Well, the 9th, the 8th, the 9th -- between the 9th and the 10th?

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Well, if you can do between the 8th and the 9th and the 9th and the 10th, that would be very helpful.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks] The night between the 8th and the 9th, in the same sector where he had spent nights before. That was in the Javor sector. And then we moved to the other side and we spent the night between the 9th and the 10th on the slopes to the north of the Three Teats and Biljeg hills.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: I don't want to be difficult but so that your markings are consistent would you just change those two so they read 8/7 and 9/7 so that we have the date of the night? Can't he rub it out?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, of course he can.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Can you just rub out -- thank you.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks] This should be erased too. This should be erased. Now you erased everything. Can I have the pen, please? [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Dragutinovic. Now can we move on, please to the combat activities of the 10th of July? Can you describe those to us briefly?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 9th, the units had already reached the Zivkovo Brdo-Rajne village line, and they stayed there at the positions that they had taken, but Combat Group 1, that consisted of a detachment, went back from Zivkovo Brdo to Zeleni Jadar to get some rest and Zivkovo Brdo was manned by a part of the Skelani Battalion. They manned the positions there. It was not a part of our tactical group. Combat Group 2, which was part of our unit, remained in the village of Rajne and to the right, in the area of the Cicevac stream.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And on the 10th?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the early morning hours of the 10th, the forces of the 28th Division launched an attack against the Combat Group 2 in the Rajne village sector, pushing it back towards the Three Teats and Biljeg hills and at the same time, in engaging elements of the Skelani Battalion, they pushed back the elements of that battalion and managed to capture the Zivkovo Brdo feature.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And what happened after that?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the afternoon, once we were able to reorganise our units, we launched a counterattack by introducing Combat Group 1, the Podrinje Detachment, along the Zeleni Jadar-Zivkovo Brdo axis, the Podrinje Detachment was able to capture Zivkovo Brdo again, and moved forwards to the village of Pusmulic and Rajne. While Combat Group 2, again in the area of the Zeleni Jadar-Srebrenica road, was able to recapture the positions that had been lost and was able to reach the Bojna village, the line there. This village is not marked here but it is closer to Srebrenica, maybe a kilometre or two closer to Srebrenica than Rajne.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: I think if we look at the road leading out of Srebrenica to the south towards Rajne and Pusmulici, we can see written alongside it the word Bojna, can't we?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can see Rajne here and Bojna is a little bit lower, but it's here where there are those hair-pin bends, and a part of this village is quite high, closer to Rajne. So if I were to mark it on the map, you would be able to see where -- how far we actually got.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Yes, please, if you would do that and then you could mark that 10/7.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, by that stage in the combat activities was there any substantial or indeed any resistance from the 28th Division forces any more?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the forces of the 28th Division did put up a very strong resistance in this fighting, and you can see from what I just told you that we suffered some casualties, but later on, when we were able to consolidate our ranks, and when we continued fighting, we were able to push them back towards Srebrenica again.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And did you spend the night in the position near Bojna? Or, rather, did the unit and Commander Pandurevic --

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We spent the night -- we spent a night in the village of Bojna, in the location that I marked, and the units were to the left and to the right of the Zeleni Jadar-Srebrenica road.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, on the 10th of July, you described to us the other day a briefing at Bojna which was conducted by General Krstic. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I do. Mr. Krstic, General Krstic, arrived to the positions that we were able to reach, and together with the commanders of Tactical Groups 1 and 2, Tactical Group 2 cooperated with us in this action, he held a briefing in order to hear reports about the tasks that were supposed to have been carried out that day, to hear to what extent they had been carried out and to discuss further tasks.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And at that briefing, did he order the deployment of an additional particular unit called the 10th Sabotage Detachment?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that the 10th Detachment was envisaged to take part in combat the next day.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Thank you. I want to just go back a little bit and ask you a couple of general questions about combat with the forces of the 28th Division. In the positions around the three hills and Biljeg, were there also -- were there also DutchBat OP positions?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On Biljeg Hill, which is not here on this map, the Dutch Battalion did have its positions. It had its positions that were set up as quarters and for combat and for observation.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And how close to the Dutch forces did the forces of the 28th Division make their positions?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were so close that we had the impression that they were actually engaging us from the positions of the Dutch Battalion.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Did you fire on any Dutch positions in the course of the combat activities of Krivaja 95?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Fire was never opened at the Dutch Battalion, but in light of the fact that the units of the 28th Division were positioned so close to the Dutch Battalion, they may have gotten the impression that fire was opened at them but no shell, no round, caused any damage to the structures of the Dutch Battalion.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Did you encounter any Dutch soldiers during the course of combat activities you were involved in?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: After taking the positions of the 28th Division in the sector of Biljeg and Three Teats, the soldiers who were the first to reach the defence lines of the 28th Division established a contact with the soldiers of the Dutch Battalion. We had a soldier who was able to talk to the Dutch in German.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And what were your orders? What were your actions towards these Dutch soldiers that you came into contact with?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, all the contacts were very correct, and a proposal was made to them to withdraw with their unit along the Zeleni Jadar-Pribicevac axis, and we told them that we would make it possible for them to go back via Pribicevac and Sase to their base in Potocari.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Thank you. One other thing: What orders did you receive in relation to destroying any property or setting fire to things and the like?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were given strict orders that no buildings were to be destroyed or set on fire, no physical damage was to be caused to any buildings in the Srebrenica area.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And who were those orders from?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From General Krstic and then Commander Pandurevic relayed them to our unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Can we now come to the 11th of July and can you describe what happened then?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 11th, pursuant to orders from the previous day, tasks were given to move towards the town of Srebrenica itself. And General Krstic himself was present.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Did you enter the town?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Tactical Group 1, including the Zvornik Brigade component, was on the Bojna-Srebrenica route, and after the first fighting started, I stayed in the area of Bojna due to NATO air strikes, and after minor injury and shell shock, I was sent back to Zeleni Jadar.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Are you aware how the forces of Tactical Group 1 were deployed on the 11th of July?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't understand the question. You mean during the attack or after we entered Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: I'm really interested in after you entered Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: After accomplishing its mission, and entering Srebrenica, the command of the Tactical Group 1 was based in the police station, whereas the other units were quartered in Gostilj village and surrounding hills in order to secure the units that remained in the town itself.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: It's correct, isn't it, that no personnel from Tactical Group 1 went towards Potocari on the 11th of July or any date thereafter?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Our outmost point towards Bratunac and Potocari was the Gostilj neighbourhood. It is on the outskirts of Srebrenica looking towards Bratunac, near the football pitch.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And where did Commander Pandurevic spend the night of the 11th of July?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To the best of my knowledge, Commander Pandurevic spent the night at the police station.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Just one last thing about the operation Krivaja 95. Was any fire from artillery that you were responsible for directed at the town of Srebrenica itself?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The town itself was not shelled by artillery, and you can see -- you could see when entering the town that there was no damage on any buildings from artillery shell.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Would you now just initial the map that's in front of you and put the date on it? You got the date wrong the last time. It's the 15th of June today, which is 15/06. But we won't worry about that.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Can the witness -- yes, he's doing it.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Now, can that be saved and preserved, but then can we call up the same exhibit for a third time? No. Can we call up 7D624 this time, please? I think that's ideal. We can just see Zepa at the bottom of the screen, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Now, what I want you to do with this map, Mr. Dragutinovic, if you can be provided with a pen, is to show the movement of the unit on the 12th, 13th, 14th and 15th of July, in the same way. So perhaps you can start by showing the movement of the unit from Srebrenica to the position where it spent the night of the 12th of July.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Thank you. And would you put 12/7 by Viogor? Thank you. That's excellent.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: We have the 12th and the 14th. Can you mark, please, the 13th for us as well?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We spent the 13th travelling non-stop, no stops for overnight rest. That was the night of the 13th. We didn't stop. This is where we spent the night on the 12th and on the 13th we started in the direction I marked and we arrived at 0200 hours on the 13th of July. Maybe I can write 13th in the area of Viogor.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you very much, if you would do that.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Now --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment, Mr. Haynes, sorry to interrupt you but we need to have the break now. We will reconvene in 25 minutes. We save this for the time being. Could you sign it, please, Mr. Dragutinovic, and put the date, today's date, 15th? In the meantime, please, can you have consultations amongst yourselves and also with the Prosecution to give us an indication where we stand? We'll reconvene in 25 minutes' time. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Haynes? Before -- have you discussed amongst yourselves --

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: We have. It might be best, I think, if the witness just slipped off his headphones for this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Mr. Dragutinovic, do you understand English?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: No, you don't. So can I ask you to remove your headphones for a short while, please? Yes, Mr. Haynes?

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: We have discussed matters. I'll say at the outset I can't give the Trial Chamber too much comfort. We are all going to use our best endeavours to be as economic in our cross-examinations and re-examinations as we can, but it appeared to us that in any event, even if I sat down now, there is enough cross-examination and re-examination of this witness to take him into next week because there are substantial cross-examinations by at least two or three of the other teams and a substantial redirect. I'm going to do my best to get through the material I've got to deal with but there are others who have placed many, many documents into e-court to use with this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Who are the others?

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: I think Madam Fauveau will cross-examine him for a considerable length of time. He is, of course, an officer within the Zvornik Brigade so he's of interest to the Nikolic team. The Beara team have asked for 45 minutes. And others have questions for him. I don't want to get into an argument about this. The witness, for my purposes, is absolutely unique and out of 187 witnesses he's the only one who was with my client from the 4th to the 15th of July, and I hope the Court would be the first to acknowledge that I'm not somebody who has abused the privilege of cross-examination in this Court. I didn't cross-examine any intercept operators, barely a survivor, and hardly any of the DutchBat officers but this witness is absolutely central to my client's case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Haynes. Our intervention was not meant to engage into any argument with any of you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I didn't really mean to but I thought for the saving of time now, I thought I would state in bullet points my position.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Madam Fauveau, how long do you expect your cross-examination to last?

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I need an hour and 45 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And Mr. Meek? You require 45 minutes as well?

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Your Honour, we had indicated that. At this point I may not have any questions depending on what the rest of the testimony is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. And -- thank you, Mr. Meek. And what sort of redirect time constraints are we talking about?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. It is at this point, I don't see it being any more than about a half an hour, so it's not quite that substantial. But that, of course, depends upon the nature of the upcoming cross-examinations.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And Mr. Haynes -- you want to cross-examine him, Ms. Nikolic?

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. We had announced one hour, but I think it's possible to reduce that to 45 minutes depending on the course of further cross-examination by Mr. Haynes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. And Mr. Haynes, how much more time do you think you require?

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: It should go a little more quickly now. Once I've asked the witness to mark a couple more things on this map, we are done with maps which are a lengthy and difficult process. There are a few documents I want to show him but I do have to take him through the remainder of the month of July up to the 23rd, and then I have to deal with the -- a portion of August and September. So I will do well to finish by the end of this session, I'd have thought.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. While incidentally the witness is not following the proceedings, in relation to the joinder motion in the Popovic case, joinder motion in the Tolimir case will be dealt with separately by Judge Prost. As far as the request for suspension of time limits for filing of response is concerned, for the time being, until further -- until you hear further from us, all time limits for filing of responses are suspended. Later on, we will have further communications for you. Let me now have some consultations with my colleagues, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Haynes, I do not mean to say to you to reduce the time for cross-examination right now but I had the impression that much of what you adduced from the -- during the course of cross-examination could have been stipulated by the Prosecution. So I would appreciate if you would pursue that path in the future.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Thank you. That's very helpful. It's certainly not something we are blind to, and Mr. McCloskey and I have good relations and are in good contact.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think you may now proceed, Mr. Haynes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Thank you. We are going to have to go back to this map just briefly, Mr. Dragutinovic. Can it be blown up to the same proportion that is it was previously and can we see the same area?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Usher, the witness is not receiving interpretation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We can put the question straight to Mr. Haynes. Do you wish to have brought up again the one that he has marked?

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Which he can put further marks upon?

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: If that is possible I would be very grateful.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think it would be better for everyone. Mr. Dragutinovic, is the interpretation now reaching you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I can hear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Now, I would just like you, if you can be provided with another pen, it can be in the same colour or a different one, it doesn't matter, just to mark a few more points for me. You told Mr. Vanderpuye about a stop during the night of the 13th and 14th when you were on the move, for fuel in Vlasenica. So would you put a circle around Vlasenica and write the word "fuel" above it or F?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And would you also put a circle around Krivace and write above that IKM?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And if you can see it, would you put a circle around Brloznik?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And would you indicate -- that was the furthest forward position that the forces made towards Zepa. You can simply say that if you agree with it.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. That is not the furthest forward position. The units had reached the line between Brloznik village and Purtic village.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: In that case, erase that circle and put a mark where that position was and perhaps write above that, TG.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Now I think we are now finished with that, so it can be saved and preserved because it already has your signature and the date upon it. Now, I want to ask you about the 13th of July. By the 13th of July, would you agree that the forces were tired, hungry and dirty?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And that many of the men who had been part of this operation by then for nine days wanted to go home?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You could say that only about Combat Group 2.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Was it the view of the commander, Pandurevic, that a replacement force ought to be used to carry out the operation towards Zepa?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I can't really remember, but I know that we were working to prepare this Combat Group 2 for the reasons I've already described so that it can continue combat activities, and there was no indication they would go back, although some individual requests and demands were made to that effect.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: You told us the other day that General Krstic mentioned to you on the 12th of July the possibility that General Mladic would address the troops on the following day, the 13th. Did you understand that the purpose of General Mladic addressing the troops was to boost their morale?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And in any event, General Krstic was aware of the possibility that General Mladic would address the troops on the 12th, that's correct, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And did you understand that the possibility of General Mladic addressing the troops was something that had been discussed at the meeting in Bratunac the previous evening, the 11th?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't know what had transpired before, but I could draw inferences from what happened on the 13th.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, you've described in some detail the protests of Colonel Pandurevic to the orders of General Mladic on the 13th of July. Did his plea not also include a plea on behalf of his tired troops?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To some extent, yes. But the way I understood it, the commander had a better idea of what the situation was really like than many others did.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Well, you've described to us in some detail the response of General Mladic to Colonel Pandurevic's protests. I mean, I assume it's fair to say that sitting here today, you don't remember the precise details of that exchange; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't recall all the details, but I remember the gist of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And the gist of it was this, wasn't it, that General Mladic was saying to Colonel Pandurevic, "Obey your orders to advance on Zepa and mind your own business in relation to the 28th Division"?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He said that Commander Pandurevic, in fact he said to Commander Pandurevic, "Did you get your assignments?" Commander Pandurevic answered yes. And then he said, "Leave the problem of the 28th Division to others. The 28th Division will not cross the Konjevic Polje-Kasaba-Milici road. Other forces will take care of that and prevent them."

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: So in effect he was saying, on the 13th of July, that the defeat or capture of the 28th Division was no responsibility of the command of the Zvornik Brigade, was it?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He didn't mention the Zvornik Brigade, only the units that were engaged in their missions and were to move towards Zepa. As for the 28th Division, other forces were supposed to take care of that but I couldn't know which other forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Thank you. I want to move on to another topic now. Did you know a man in the Zvornik Brigade called Dragan Stevic?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And would you agree that throughout this period certainly, he was Vinko Pandurevic's driver?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And it's correct, isn't it, that throughout the period you have described and marked on this map, you were travelling in the same vehicle as Vinko Pandurevic?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. For the most part. I wasn't with him always but I mostly was with him. There were certain errands I had to take care of.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: But certainly you were with him on the journey that went through the night of the 13th to 14th of July when you stopped for fuel at Vlasenica?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Now, the stop for fuel in Vlasenica involved a long convoy of vehicles, didn't it?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And you may not recall this but we'll have a look at a couple of documents, but it was a refueling stop that began before midnight on the 13th of July and finished in the small hours of the morning on the 14th. That's right, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Replenishment took a long time because it was a small local petrol station where we refueled the whole base of the VRS.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Thank you for that but in any event, I just want you to have a quick look to remind yourself at P177. Can that be placed into e-court, please? And can we see that that is a fueling document that's initially dated the 13th of July at the top?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. 13th July 1995. You see it in the left top corner.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: But in relation to the fueling of the vehicles, as each entry is signed by the driver on the right, it's become the 14th. So the document began to be filled in on the 13th but then proceeded by people dating it the 14th as they filled their vehicles. That's right? And I want you to have a look just quickly at vehicle number 13.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and you see the signature of Stevic, Dragan.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Thank you very much indeed. 48 litres of fuel, and if we just look --

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It started on the 13th and it ended after midnight. So he wrote the actual date when he tanked up.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Thank you. And after you'd fueled up, you and Vinko Pandurevic and Dragan Stevic got back in that car and drove on towards Pozeplje?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And where precisely did you spend the night that night?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were in Rijeka village, between Pozeplje and Han Pijesak.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: In what sort of building?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were no buildings, just an abandoned house. Everybody spent the night the best way they could. Some under tent. Some in their vehicles. I think most people slept in their cars. Many more than in the house.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And you and the commander? Were you together in the same building?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. In the house, in the car, or around the car. I had one tent that I stretched between the car and a nearby tree, just in case it rained.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: I just want to be absolutely clear about this. On the nights of the 12th, 13th and 14th of July, you can confirm that Vinko Pandurevic was with you and the unit on the route that you drew on that map?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely, and certainly.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Now, throughout the period of the 4th to the 15th of July, consistent with the procedure you described yesterday, Dragan Obrenovic was in command of the Zvornik Brigade, that's correct, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And in the absence of the commander, he would command, subject to the orders of higher command; that's also correct, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And he's answerable to the superior command.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And I would just like to show you a couple of documents so that we can see that process in action in the relevant period, and can we have placed into e-court now, please, P438? Take a little time to read this, but this, I think you'll agree, is an order from Drina Corps command on the 11th of July to strengthen combat readiness of the units and an order that all forward command posts had to be upgraded on all levels? The document may need to go down a little bit so that the witness can read it and confirm that. It's really the second half of the document.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Basically I'm familiar with it. Without even reading it, I can see what it's about.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And just a second document, P157. You perhaps should clear this up. You do confirm that without even reading it, my summary of the document was accurate, the first document you saw?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. You said what is written, so I didn't need to read it, but this thing I do have to read. Yes. I read it. This has to do with the task for the Zvornik Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And the date of the order?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it's difficult to read the date here. I think it's the 12th of July.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Thank you. So these were orders, both of them addressed to Zvornik Brigade command in the absence of the commander, Vinko Pandurevic?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Now, during the time you were away in Srebrenica and Zepa, the commander, Vinko Pandurevic, never gave any order to the Zvornik Brigade, did he?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is true because the commander, according to the order, was the commander of the tactical group and he was duty-bound to command this unit and only that unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And more to the point, he wasn't notified of any orders that had been given to the Zvornik Brigade by higher command, was he?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. We had certain tasks and there was no need for us to be even informed about this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Vanderpuye?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I object to the question, and frankly to the answer as well, because the basis of knowledge hasn't been established with respect to what information this witness would have had of his commander's orders.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Oh, I think it has. I think Mr. Vanderpuye established in his examination-in-chief that this man was with, spoke to and asked about everything that was going through Vinko Pandurevic's mind,, and I will deal with it in that way if Mr. Vanderpuye insists but I'll move on. The question has been answered.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. We agree with your submission, Mr. Haynes. Go ahead. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Now, during the time you were in Srebrenica and Zepa, you didn't have, yourself, any information about the evacuation of prisoners, the transportation of prisoners, or the execution of prisoners, did you?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Yes, what you said is correct. I didn't know anything. I didn't hear about any such things.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And just to make sure the foundation is good, you travelled with Vinko Pandurevic in his car, that's correct, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: You slept with him at night, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: You regularly conversed with him about the combat situation and the general situation in the Srebrenica and surrounding areas?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And received orders.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And to your knowledge, Vinko Pandurevic had no knowledge of the evacuation, transportation or execution of prisoners during the period that you were involved in combat operations with him?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I never had any feeling that the commander knew anything about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, in terms of the involvement of Zvornik Brigade personnel in Operation Krivaja 95, it's correct, isn't it, that a number of soldiers were decorated for their bravery in Operation Krivaja 95?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And I'd like you to quickly look at 7D440, please. And it's page 2, entries 18 to 21. This is the list of people decorated and there appear to have been four from the Zvornik Brigade who were decorated; do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know the man listed under number 18. I know the man listed under number 20 personally. I also know the man under number 22. And I could perhaps find other people that I know, if I were to look, to go through this list in detail.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: It might help you if the list was just moved to the right a bit so you could see the units that these people were part of. It needs to go a bit further than that. And we --

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. From 18 and then onwards, these are all members of the Zvornik Infantry Brigade but if you're asking me if I knew some of these people personally, then, yes, I did but according to this list they belong to the Zvornik Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Thank you. And I wonder if lastly you could just look at the very last page of this document so that that we could see the number of people who were decorated in total. And you can confirm that the number is 60 of which apparently 4 were from the Zvornik Brigade?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. 60, as listed here.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, I'd like to move on to your return to Zvornik from Zepa. And just to clear up one thing. After your unit returned from Zepa on the 15th of July, it's correct, isn't it, that no unit or personnel of the Zvornik Brigade returned to the operation towards Zepa before the 31st of July?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. The plan was for a part of the Podrinje Detachment to do so on the 23rd but then an order was received later on that they were to go on.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: But so that we are clear, that they didn't in fact go until the 31st of July?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In fact, they went on the 31st, and on the 1st they were there, and perhaps for one more day, and not before that.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, you're familiar, I imagine, with the brigade forward command post at Delici.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And you're familiar, I imagine, with the fact that from the forward command post, there is a very good view of the positions of the 4th, 6th and 7th Battalions and an effective position to command each of those units.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And that's why it was chosen, because it was possible to monitor the other battalions from there, the 3rd, the 2nd, the 5th and the 1st to a smaller degree, but all the battalions could be observed from there. There was a line of sight to all of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And also, there was a very good line of sight to the villages of Nezuk, Drugi Dijo [phoen] and the positions of the 2nd Corps of the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. There was a line of sight to the village of Nezuk. It was just opposite the forward command post, in a northerly direction.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Now, although you weren't back in Zvornik until the 15th of July, you have seen, as operations officer, all of the regular and irregular combat reports of July of 1995, that's correct, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: After the return, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And you are aware from that and from your presence there, from the 15th of July onwards, that the Zvornik Brigade, in Baljkovica and Crni Vrh, had strong forces in the 7th and the 4th Battalion; two platoons from the Bircanska Light Infantry Brigade; a platoon of military police; a platoon from the Krajina Corps; a platoon from Vlasenica; a special MUP brigade from Sekovici; Drina Wolves; tank company; and strong artillery support from the Zvornik Brigade?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. They were all stationed there in the period of the 15th, 16th, 17th and 18th. And even before that, some elements had arrived already on the 14th.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And those forces, in the positions that they were placed, effectively commanded from the forward command post, would have been quite sufficient to massacre the column of the 28th Division and the civilians coming from the rear, wouldn't they?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The commander from his command post was able to exercise command very easily, and this strength of units was quite sufficient to inflict major casualties on the 28th Division, in particular if they had civilians with them.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Now, it is correct that the Zvornik Brigade suffered some losses on the 15th and 16th of July?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. It did have some losses in those days, and even before, in the period before the Tactical Group 1 had arrived from Srebrenica and Zepa.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Would you agree that in the period of the 15th and 16th of July, there were a lot of armed men congregated in a relatively small geographical area?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The sector of the 4th Battalion in terms of the lay of the land, was in a valley, and all the features that dominated the valley had been taken before or were taken now by the Zvornik Brigade, in particular the 7th Battalion Pandurica, the 6th Battalion to the right, Parlog, and then in the depth, from the Zvornik-Caparde road, from the Crni Vrh sector, the units from already advancing towards Cetino Brdo which is a dominant hill. It dominates this entire area.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Is it right that some of the losses that were suffered by the brigade in that period could be accounted for by the concentration of armed men in a small area who fell victim to random and even friendly fire?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was a really small area, and the possibility for conflicts and even friendly fire, it was quite rife, in fact, in this small area.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Now, I assume you have heard of Semso Muminovic?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I've heard.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And you were aware that your commander was in contact with him from the brigade forward command post during the period, I will suggest, of the 15th and 16th of July?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I know, through the commander of the 7th Battalion, because I had direct contacts with him, and the commander of the 7th Battalion was in contact with the commander at the forward command post.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Did he let you know the regularity of that contact? Were you aware that there were many, many phone calls between them over a 24-hour period or so?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From my contacts with the commander of the 7th Battalion, I do know that the contacts were first established on the 15th and that they ended on the 16th, with the final agreement about letting the 28th Division and the civilian population that accompanied it through.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And did you see the column pass?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, in part, what could be observed from Pandurica, which was a dominant feature. But I was able to see the size of the column as I passed with the armoured mechanised company going in the direction of Zvornik and Caparde.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And could you see that the column contained both armed and unarmed men?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the Pandurica position, it was impossible to ascertain whether people were armed or unarmed. One could only see whether they were soldiers or in civilian clothes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And could you see that some of them were soldiers?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, for sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Now, you've told us a little bit the other day about a colonel called Trkulja. Were you aware that he visited the command of the Zvornik Brigade as part of a group of officers?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that he was present only on the basis of the conversation or at least that's what the situation was like at the time, with the logistics detachment soldiers who gave me, relayed to me an order, what I should do as a next task, and intimating that there was a high-ranking officer at the command but he didn't know who he was, so I didn't insist on identifying that man, but I was able to see from the documents that I saw later who that officer was, because in the duty operations officer's notebook, and in the duty operations officer logbook, it is stated quite clearly who the officer was and what time he was there.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Thank you. Well, I just want to clarify with you what date that was, and to that end I'm going to show you P378, please. And it's page 89 for the witness, page 4 for those of us who read English.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: A soldier or, rather, the platoon leader handed to me the order of the commander, and that was in the afternoon of the 17th.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I've just -- I'm just showing you now a page from the duty operations officer's logbook for the 17th of July, and does that show that at 8.45, that morning, a team of officers headed by Colonel Trkulja stayed in the brigade IKM for insight of the new situation, the same returned at 1500 hours?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. To analyse the situation in those days and in those operations, it says here 8.45. This is indeed an excerpt from the logbook and it bears the signature of an officer but I can't recognise whose signature it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Did you understand that the purpose of the arrival of those officers was to investigate why your commander had allowed the column to pass?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the basis of what I learned later, the purpose of their arrival was to check why the commander had, on his own initiative, decided to let the column pass through our ranks, through our combat positions.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: 1995 wasn't the first time that you heard of Semso Muminovic, was it?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I knew Semso Muminovic from before the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And it wasn't the only time that he and Vinko Pandurevic resolved a conflict situation by cease-fire and allowing men to go free?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were instances before. Mr. Pandurevic and Mr. Muminovic had been in contact before regarding some exchanges and so on. I do remember that; I'm quite sure of that. Even before this event on the 15th, 16th and the 17th.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And on a similar but different level, in Ustipraca in 1993, Commander Pandurevic had reached an agreement with the opposing Muslim forces to allow substantial number of their soldiers to walk free to the free territory then, hadn't he?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It's true. I was there with the commander and the commander was the commander of the tactical group that included units of the Zvornik Brigade and of the Rogatica brigade and the 2nd Romanija Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Thank you. After the passage of the column, it's right that the Zvornik Brigade was tasked to perform a search of the terrain to determine whether there were armed groups left behind and groups that had infiltrated from the 2nd Corps of the Bosnian army, that's right, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That's right. Quite a few armed soldiers of the 28th Division were left behind and they constantly tried to break through, not only in this segment but in other areas, to get in the rear of our units where conflicts would break out. The command was forced to search the terrain to prevent any attacks by those straggling groups on our units at the defence line.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And that search of the terrain in the days following the 17th of July resulted in the capture of a large number of enemy soldiers, didn't it?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were prisoners, not a large number, but I do have an approximate figure.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Those prisoners were all detained in the military prison at the barracks at Standard in Karakaj, weren't they?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. On the orders of the commander, all the soldiers of the 28th Division who surrendered were handed over to military police squads who took them to the barracks where they were placed in detention until they could be transported to the collection centre for the prisoners at Batkovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And the prisoners at the barracks were mixed, weren't they, with prisoners of the Zvornik Brigade who were being held there for military offences?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, we really couldn't keep them apart, but there were no major problems as a result of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And Commander Pandurevic asked superior command to transport these prisoners so that the exchange process could be begun with them?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I didn't really understand your question, but I do get the gist. The procedure for the capture of the enemy troops by the Zvornik Brigade was well known. The prisoners were to be taken to the barracks, there to be placed in detention, and the next day or the day after that, at the latest, they were to be taken to Batkovic. As for the exchange, the Zvornik Brigade did not have the capability to carry out such exchanges on its own.
