There was a commission that was in charge of exchanging the enemy soldiers for our soldiers who had been captured by the other side. But I do know about this case that you, I think, are referring to. But if you get more specific, I will be able to tell you what I know.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Yes. It would be far easier if I just showed you the document I had in mind. It's P340, please. Can that be placed into e-court? Is that a document in your handwriting?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That's my document and my handwriting. In fact, it's the commander's document but written by me.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Thank you for the correction. I think we need to go down the document so that you can identify the section of the document that deals with the question of exchange of prisoners.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I remember well, it's like this: During these combat operations in the area of Baljkovica, Memici, some of our soldiers went missing, some were captured. From the communications between the enemy and our command, through Muminovic and Pandurevic, there were some indications that they were in favour of direct exchange for some of their soldiers who had been captured and who they knew to be still on our side. As for our soldiers who had been captured and were on the other side, their families found out about it somehow and pressured us a great deal to accept the exchange. However, we had no authorisation to do that. Therefore, we asked the corps command to hand down some instructions or to send a commission for exchange if they thought that was the best thing to do. Otherwise, we needed them to tell us what to do with the prisoners, to wait for the commission or to send them on to Batkovici.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Does that explain why at paragraph 3 of this interim combat report the commander is requesting that corps command and -- requests that corps command ask the exchange commission to start work as soon as possible?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. Precisely. The commander asked for instructions so that we wouldn't have any more problems. And the commission was needed to start working immediately.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Now, we've gone a little forward in time. I want now to go back to the 18th of July, if I can. And I'd like for P334 to be placed into e-court. This is another interim combat report of the 18th of July, and do you recall whether or not this is another report that was dictated to you by the commander, Vinko Pandurevic?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. By that time, I had already returned to the command sometime in the afternoon, and I'm familiar with this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: I'd like it, please, if the document could go to the very bottom to see if you can clear something up for us.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Which paragraph?

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: It needs to go right to the bottom, to the commander's signature. It will be another page. And if we could zoom in on the signature box? Now --

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That's the commander's signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Thank you. Now on the 18th of July, what time was it that you went to have this document dictated to you by the commander?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the afternoon, but I couldn't tell you the hour.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Well, in the English translation, this document is timed 1317. That's 1.00 in the afternoon. Is that in your view --

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. It must have been later.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: I mean, it could be an 8. Is it more likely that this document was timed 1817? In other words, just after quarter past 6.00 in the evening?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's certainly not 13. But later.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, is this a document you recall being dictated to you?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And do you recall the mood of the commander at the time he dictated this document to you?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All these events, in view of the fact that the commander had taken many responsibilities upon himself and made his own decisions, he was rather angry with the superior command, that is, with the Drina Corps command.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: This document, particularly if we can go back to the first page and look at paragraph 4, does not contain language that -- the like of which we generally find in combat reports from the Zvornik Brigade, does it?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And to put it into its context, it was written a day after Colonel Pandurevic had been visited by the three colonels from the Main Staff; you recall that?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was on the 18th, from what I know, and they came before.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: I don't want to be difficult but it's probably my fault. We've flicked about this document. I just wonder whether it could be taken down so that the witness can see the whole document, to understand my next questions. Can we go to paragraph 4? The next page, please. From the top, please. Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Further down.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I see this paragraph.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Would you agree that the commander took the opportunity in this document to include every piece of information at his disposal about brigade losses from March of 1995 right up to the day of writing that report?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In this passage that I see on the screen, I don't see that. I see paragraph 4, though.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: I think it needs to go further up. No, the other way. Maybe back a page.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think this document has more than two pages.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Thank you. When that document has been taken down a little bit so you can see the three sections of losses that it contains, I'll put the question again. Can it go down a little further?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Thank you. And a bit more. Can we see the last section, please? Now, I'll put the question to you again. In this report, Commander Pandurevic took the opportunity, didn't he, to convey to corps command every piece of information he had about brigade losses pretty much in the whole of 1995 but certainly most recently?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is from the 27th March, when Zvornik Brigade was involved in intensive fighting quite apart from Krivaja 95, and sustained considerable losses. The point of all this is to inform the corps command of the problems that the Zvornik Brigade was facing, and all the tasks that we received from the superior command outside the area of defence of the Zvornik Brigade. We were trying to make a point that it was very questionable whether we would be able to accomplish all these tasks.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Thank you. And in order to be persuasive when he was dictating these figures to you, he was trying to make the situation look as bad as possible, wasn't he?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it couldn't have been worse. These figures are something that I'm aware of.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And did you, at the time that you were listening to him telling you what to write, understand that he thought he was under some suspicion from superior command because of his actions on the 16th and 17th in letting the column go?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At any rate, Commander Pandurevic was then under fire from the superior command because he had on his own initiative taken the decision to let the column pass through their positions. I know that for sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Now, before we leave this document, I just want to deal with a separate point with you, and can we go, please, now, to the first paragraph of the document? There is a description there, isn't there, of the way in which or the determination with which some members of the 28th Division fought even after capture?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: A document written on the 18th of July; did you ever receive on the 18th of July any order from Vinko Pandurevic that captured soldiers were to be shot rather than taken prisoner?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I arrived at the brigade command sometime in the afternoon on the 18th. I know about this document. I also know that the stragglers of the 28th Division fought to the last in order to be able to pass through, to break out, and we learned from those we captured that many of them were ready to die and commit suicide before surrendering but I had never heard from the commander that we were not taking any prisoners or that we should kill those who surrender.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Leave aside from the commander, did you ever hear of any such order?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Never. I never heard any such thing. That's what I'm trying to tell you. From the 18th when I returned to the brigade, I never heard the commander say any such thing. I know only about the order to boost security measures to be applied during capturing and search of terrain, but that does not mean killing prisoners.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Thank you very much, indeed. And I'm going to ask you a question you volunteered the answer to a little while ago. About how many prisoners were taken, detained and sent for exchange by the Zvornik Brigade in the period after the 17th of July up to the 22nd?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to the records that I had at the time, and the records of the duty operations logbook and the combat reports we sent to the corps, and from my personal knowledge, there were around 80 men taken prisoner.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Thank you. And in your experience generally in the Zvornik Brigade, were prisoners of war treated fairly, properly and in accordance with the Geneva Conventions?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Those men that were taken prisoner by the Zvornik Brigade were treated precisely like that. I can give you an example that happened in my presence. Soldiers brought 12 troops of the 28th Division who had been captured, they were all in shiny new uniforms, all young, fit. All of them were offered food and water. Some accepted, some refused. Some accepted a smoke. Our soldiers struck up a conversation with them, and to be frank, it all seemed a bit unreal after what had been going on for the past month.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I'm about to move on to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Haynes, before you go on, you dealt with extensively with this exhibit but I had the impression that not much was asked about paragraph 4 to the witness. Mr. Dragutinovic, I wonder if you read paragraph 4 in full. I think it's on the second page. If the e-court shows the page 4 -- page 2, para 4.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: While we are going there can I make a cross-inquiry. I'm a bit disoriented; when are we due another break?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Half past.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: In about 20 minutes' time. Unless you require it earlier.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: No, no, no, no. I know we rose a little early.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But we also understand the stress of cross-examination. We've all been lawyers before.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Any time you need a break, Mr. Haynes, just -- that equally applies to you, Witness. Any time you need a break, please let us know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Dragutinovic, I'd like to know in particular what the situation was as you understood it, in particular in relation to those 3.000 Muslim prisoners.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I first heard of 3.000 captured Muslims from the commander, that is from that document that the commander dictated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: What was your understanding at the time what happened to those prisoners? What did you know and did you know why your commander was upset?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I did not understand it that way. I didn't think that the commander was upset. I still believe, and I assert, that he was very angry with the superior command because somebody had decided to bring to the Zvornik municipality 3.000, as it says here, captives, and to allow 7.000, which I read as 7.000 soldiers of the 28th Division, simply to find themselves behind the lines of the Zvornik Brigade, behind the back of the Zvornik Brigade. He says it is inconceivable in this text.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. I'm referring to those 3.000 Muslim prisoners. Did you or did you not know at the time what happened to those 3.000 Muslim prisoners?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I thought that those 3.000 prisoners were put up somewhere. At that time, I wasn't aware that they were there until the moment when this was dictated. It says here they were put up in school-houses, and elsewhere on the territory of the Zvornik municipality. And that's what I believed. Because I had no occasion to see for myself what was going on between the 11th and my return to the brigade command.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: When did you know at the end of the day those prisoners were executed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I had never personally, from documents or from talking to other people, found out where, how and how many soldiers or civilians who had been captured during all these events from Srebrenica to Zvornik were executed. And there are some reasons that could explain that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. I'll stop here. I'll leave it to the parties.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Haynes?

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Thank you, Judge Kwon.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: I was going to move on now to the period in August and September, when you went on a separate operation with your commander, Vinko Pandurevic. You'll remember, I imagine, that at the beginning of August, Drina Corps command ordered the formation of a light infantry brigade called the Drinski Brigade, to carry out operations in the Krajina, in the area of Drvar?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Just so that we get the dates correct, I'm going to ask that you're briefly shown 7D612. And is that an order of Drina Corps command dated the 3rd of August of 1995, ordering the formation of a light infantry brigade called the Drinski Brigade to be commanded by Colonel Pandurevic?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That's the order we received from the superior command.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And I'd like you quickly to look at some other documents now. 7D252. Again, briefly look at it, a document dated the 6th of August. It's an order on behalf of the Drinski Brigade, and if we go to the bottom, we can see who gave that order. I think we might need a second page.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that's already a document that governs the establishment of that brigade, and the commander is designated. Lieutenant-Colonel Vinko Pandurevic is appointed commander. I'm familiar with this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And this second document I've shown you is a document dated the 6th of August showing Vinko Pandurevic already issuing orders as commander of that brigade; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And according to your understanding of the position, from the 6th of August he was commander of the Drinski Brigade and therefore ceased to act as commander of the Zvornik Brigade?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct. Because by assuming command over that newly formed brigade, the commander no longer commands the Zvornik Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And do you recall that, in fact, you gave the orders to march in relation to that brigade?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. In that command, I was appointed again operations officer and pursuant to the commander's order, the commander of the brigade, I drafted that order to march, designated the routes and formulated all the other components of such a document.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Do you remember, in fact, that the Drinski Brigade marched to Krajina on the 7th of August, the day after this and other orders were given by Vinko Pandurevic?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. The march started on the 7th.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And I'm going to a little more carefully deal with the date of your return. I'd like, please, if you could be shown P378, the bottom of page 121 and the top of page 122. This is going to be a little difficult, Mr. Dragutinovic. You're going to have to read the bottom of one page and then wait for another page to come up. It is the very bottom of the page you're looking at and now can we look at page 122 at the very top? I should say by way of introduction that this is the duty officer's logbook for the 16th of September.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, right below that, right below this first line, it says, "Today at 11.30, that 2nd Drina Brigade," that's what we call it, "returned to Zvornik headed by Lieutenant-Colonel Vinko Pandurevic, from the area of responsibility of the 2nd Krajina Corps." The date is the 16th, 11.30.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Thank you very much. This is the duty officer's logbook and as you told us yesterday, this is a document that summarises and puts into some sort of chronology information from the notebook and perhaps other sources; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That's from the notebook of the duty operations officer and then it was copied into the logbook. In fact, this is the logbook.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Thank you. And the passage I asked you to read at the bottom of page 121, which appears to have occurred or have been written in any way before the entry about the return of the 2nd Drina Brigade concerns the commander inspecting positions of the 7th Battalion in the village of Memici, do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the first part?

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And the reference to the commander in the first part of the logbook for the 16th of September must therefore refer to Dragan Obrenovic, mustn't it?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Dragan Obrenovic was the commander at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: So that we can draw this together, the 2nd Drina Brigade was in Krajina from the 7th of August until 11.30 in the morning of the 16th of September?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And at the time of its return, the deputy commander, called commander at the time, of the Zvornik Brigade was inspecting positions of the 7th Battalion in Memici?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes. Dragan Obrenovic, as the brigade commander in the absence of Commander Pandurevic, performed all the relevant duties. We came back at that time, when Dragan Obrenovic was already at the other end of the brigade's defence area.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And just to give this particular passage of evidence a human element, you came back with Vinko Pandurevic, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I came back, and upon my return, the commander called up the command to meet at the command post of the Zvornik Brigade at Karakaj where we summed up some reports and we gave some tasks to the members of the command so that some of the units that were part of the Drina Brigade would be able to go back to their original units smoothly, without any problems.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: But when you got back to Standard, there was no question of Dragan Obrenovic being there and briefing Vinko Pandurevic on the situation within the Zvornik Brigade, was there?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't recall that we actually found him there at the barracks.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Dragutinovic. And that would be a convenient moment for a break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you so much, Mr. Haynes. We'll have a 25-minute break. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Haynes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Now, just before we broke, Mr. Dragutinovic, you were explaining to us both from your own personal recollection and by reference to some of the brigade documents, about your return from the Krajina with Vinko Pandurevic on the 16th of September. I want to try and link that with another important event in this case. And I'd like you to tell us, please, if you recall a man called Radislav Pantic, who was the chief of traffic services within the logistics organ of the Zvornik Brigade. Yes?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know who Pantic is and I do know him. He was the chief of the traffic service in the logistics organ of the brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And I wonder if we could now put into e-court please P1054. Could the document be brought down a little bit so that we can see the top right-hand corner? No, probably -- I meant brought up, yes. Yes. Now, can you see that on that document, the name Pantic is written in the top right-hand corner?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And can you see that that document is a document from the Main Staff to the Drina Corps notifying them of an order of the Main Staff for the delivery to the Drina Corps of 5.000 litres of diesel?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you could maybe scroll down a little bit?

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Of course. That will be done for you.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, I can see that now.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Just one thing about that document: A copy of it appears to have come to the Zvornik Brigade, but for information. What does that mean, when a document is given to the Drina Corps for information?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know what it means if Zvornik Brigade received it for information. That means that this fuel belongs to someone and that perhaps it could be stored in a facility somewhere, but that Pantic or the Zvornik Brigade is just provided with this for information. It cannot avail itself of it. It cannot dispose of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Thank you. And would you just make a mental note of the confidential document number 03/4-2341 of the 14th of September? And then I'm going to ask you to look, please, at P1053. And can you see straight away, if you've remembered it, in the top left-hand -- no, we haven't got the document up yet. Yes, in the top left-hand corner we have the same order number there, 03/4-2341. And again, the document marked Pantic in the top right-hand corner. And this is a telegram dated the 14th of September, again from the -- what's described here as the General Staff to the electronic communications centre -- sorry, addressed to the logistics -- to the 1st Zvornik Brigade for their information. Now, I want now to look, if we can, at P379 which is the duty officer's notebook at page 115, and this is only in your language, Mr. Dragutinovic. There is no English translation so we may have to have your help with it.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I am able to read it.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Well, I certainly can't so you're better placed than I am. Can the document be brought up so he can see the lower half of the page? And can you see there, there is an asterisk relating to a telegram?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And again, it contains the same number. Would you mind please just reading out what you can there so that we can have something on the record in English?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says, "Telegram, strictly confidential, 03/4-2341, dated the 14th of September 1995. And telegram strictly confidential number 10/34/2-3-701, dated the 14th of September." It says 9 here but I assume that this refers to the year 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me just try and see what it says further on. I don't really see whether it says, "Handed in to Pantic." It says, "To be handed over to Pantic."

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Thank you very much. And if we could just go to the top of the page, I think we'll see that this is again the 14th of July. Thank you. There, on the top right-hand -- sorry, 14th of September. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Now, while you were in the Krajina with Vinko Pandurevic, which trip you returned from on the 16th of July, were you ever aware of any --

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Were you ever aware of any arrangement between the Main Staff of the army of Republika Srpska and the Drina Corps for the delivery of 500 litres of fuel?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Except on the basis of what I've just read now.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And again, did you enjoy the same sort of relationship with Commander Pandurevic during the time that you were in the Krajina that you had done when you were on Operation Krivaja 95? In other words, did you stay with him? Did you travel with him? Did you talk to him?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was the commander's operations officer, and on both occasions, I was by the commander's side precisely in order to receive orders, to work them out, and to convey them to the units, which means that I was at the commander's side at all times.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And did anything that you discussed or anything he said indicate to you that he had any knowledge of an arrangement being made for the delivery of fuel by the Main Staff to the Drina Corps to be stored at the barracks of the Zvornik Brigade during your absence in the Krajina?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: During our stay in Krajina, we had such problems that fuel for the Zvornik Brigade and for Standard was not a topic that we could have discussed even if we had wanted to.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Now, I want to come back, please, to the 16th of September and your return to the Zvornik Brigade command. You've told us that on the 16th of September, when Colonel Pandurevic returned, he dealt with substantially the return of the other units to their respective brigades and that so far as you were aware, he had no contact with Dragan Obrenovic that day. I want to have a look now at the following day, the 17th of September, and can we look, please, at P379, at page 122? I'm very sorry, I might have made a mistake here. We have to start on page 121. I'm very sorry to the Court usher, who is doing a great job. Can we try page 122 again? I'm sorry about this, the 65 ter number at the top -- the ERN number at the top should be 6530. Yes. And could you help us, please, by reading the top lines there? Because I think we might need to see a little bit of the previous page. Mr. Dragutinovic, would you help us, please, by just reading out those top lines and seeing if they make any sense?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can see it says here, "Lieutenant-Colonel Pandurevic should maybe upon arrival in Vlasenica report to General Krstic".

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And then?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "And in the afternoon, he should not go to Vlasenica." That's what I read but I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, this is the day after the --

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I understand that somebody ordered Commander Pandurevic to go to Vlasenica and then, in the second part, on the orders of General Krstic, he should not go to Vlasenica because probably something or other had been cancelled. So there was no need for him to go.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, the day prior to this, Colonel Pandurevic had returned with the 1st Drina Brigade which had been ordered by the Drina Corps. Now, would it have been protocol for him to report to General Krstic, the commander of the Drina Corps, upon returning with that brigade?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it would be logical, but not on that day. He didn't go on that day. I know that for sure. Not to brief, but to make a report; he could have done that in writing. And let me just add on this note that I drafted the reports on the stay of the Zvornik Brigade in Krajina.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, just beneath that entry is a telephone number, and a further entry. I wonder if you could read that out to us?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says here, "589-991." I can't read what it says here in the middle but then it says, "In Celopek." Something like, "I am now in Celopek" or something like that. No, it says, "589-991, lieutenant-colonel in Celopek."

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Thank you. Now Celopek and the telephone number 589-9991 [sic], does that mean anything to you?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Should I say? It's a private number of a person where the commander was.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Thank you, and just lastly, the next entry says what?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Below this, "Major in" - I'd say Malesic - "at a briefing." Or something like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This probably refers to Major Dragan Obrenovic indicating that he was in Malesic at the briefing, most likely in one of the battalions or something like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Now, I'll ask you again: Do you have any independent recollection of the events of the 17th of September that might help us supplement what the notebook means?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What do you mean specifically? The same image or something else? Is there something else that you're referring to?

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Again, Mr. Dragutinovic, you're quite right to criticise my questions. Can I suggest to you that what the notebook shows us is that on the 17th of September, Lieutenant-Colonel Pandurevic was at a house in Celopek, that he had --

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: That Major Dragan Obrenovic was in Malesici?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Malesic, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And that Lieutenant-Colonel Pandurevic had no obligation, at that stage, to go to Vlasenica?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He did not have such an obligation because in the previous entry, it is stated that he didn't need to go to Vlasenica, because a commander would not have gone to Celopek on his own initiative. He would go to carry out his task. So this indicates quite clearly that the commander was -- had taken some kind of a leave of absence. He was resting.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Thank you. And there is one further minor point about this. It's unusual, isn't it, that the commander and the Chief of Staff are referred to in the notebook by their military rank? They are referred to here as lieutenant-colonel and major, not as commander or Chief of Staff.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I have to tell you that every officer made the kind of notes that he found the easiest, the most convenient. These were not professional soldiers, where everything has to be done in accordance with the rules just so.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Very well. I'll take that no further. But are you aware that on the 17th of September, Commander Pandurevic was given leave of absence by General Krstic to --

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He was granted leave of absence because of some health problems that he had.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And if we can now look at P379, at page 128, and that's the relevant part that is on the screen now, again, there is a telephone number there, and a reference to a room number, and the name of the commander. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It's quite obvious that the commander had already left. Let me just explain. The commander had some problems with his back. The year before he had had surgery, back surgery, and he'd already had some problems while we were in Krajina. So this is the telephone number, and I guess the room in the hotel where he was staying.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And do you know where that hotel was?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it was in Montenegro somewhere.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, later on in the month of September, were you aware that Dragan Obrenovic was asked to command a unit to go to Krajina?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I do know about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: I think originally, the unit was to be led by Colonel Furtula of whom we have heard -- Trkulja of whom we've heard previously but when he was unable to do it for various reasons the Drina Corps asked Dragan Obrenovic to take his place?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me correct you here. If I'm not mistaken I think this was Colonel Furtula.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: I got it right the first time but then I corrected myself and got it wrong. It was Radomir Furtula, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, if it's Radomir, then that could be Furtula, and I know him quite well so I couldn't have made a mistake. He was appointed the commander of that unit. First for some reasons he was not, then he was. And then he was actually -- actually Major Obrenovic was invited to receive the task.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, just so that we can ascertain the date or relevant dates, could we look at P158, please? And is this the order appointing Dragan Obrenovic as commander of this unit dated the 26th of September of 1995?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, precisely. That's the document confirming what I've just said, that Radomir Furtula was the man and then Major Dragan Obrenovic was tasked with setting up the brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Thank you. And just to follow this through, throughout the period from the 17th of September to the 26th of September, when this order was made, Dragan Obrenovic was the commander of the Zvornik Brigade; that's correct, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. By virtue of his office, he was the deputy commander of the brigade, and he took over the command of the brigade until the 26th, when the commander returned to the brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Well, I'm just going to see if we can clarify that. Can we look, please, at Exhibit 37 -- P379 again, page 140? And can we have a look at the entry at 10.00, 1000 hours? Does that refer to a briefing of the battalion and division commanders?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It says here under 1000 hours, yes, precisely.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And we can see at the top of this page that this refers to the 27th of September. Now, that debriefing would have been, wouldn't it, the debriefing held by the commander on his return to the command on that day?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The briefing of the battalion and artillery battalion commanders is always held in the presence of the commander. In his absence, it is done in the presence of the Chief of Staff. So this means that the commander was present there because Major Obrenovic had already taken on the tasks to set up this brigade that he was supposed to take to Krajina.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, can we just summarise the movement of the commander that you've taken us through? On the 7th of August he departed for the Krajina, returning on the 16th of September; that's correct, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: On neither the 16th nor the 17th, did he resume command of the brigade, nor did he have any contact with Dragan Obrenovic?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know if he did or not, but he was given leave of absence starting the very next day, and he left the very next day.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And he returned when Dragan Obrenovic went off to command another unit on either the 26th or the 27th of September?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. On the 26th and on the 27th, the commander was already in the brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: So to all intents and purposes, the commander of the Zvornik Brigade was Dragan Obrenovic from the 7th of August to the 26th or 27th of September?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Now, were you yourself ever aware of 500 litres of fuel being stored -- sorry, 5.000 litres of fuel being stored at the barracks at Standard?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I never heard about such a quantity of fuel being stored in our barracks.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Did you ever see such a quantity of fuel --

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not see it and I did not have to know.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And I just want to show you a few images now, please. Can we see P171 -- sorry, P2103, at page 171? Do you know the dam at Petkovci?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know the dam well because my construction company worked there, but if this image depicts the dam, I do not distinguish it.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Well, let me put a simple question to you. These images are intended to show that sometime between the 7th of September 1995 and the 27th of September 1995, some bodies were dug up at the dam at Petkovci. Were you at that time aware of anything like that going on?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I was never aware of any excavations. I never learned that from any source.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And again, a question I've asked you two or three times: So far as you were aware, could Vinko Pandurevic know anything of any such engineering operations?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In which period?

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Well, between the 7th and the 27th of September would be pretty important.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No way. Because we were not at all in the area of defence of the Zvornik Brigade. We were in Krajina. We were engaged in completely different missions. I'm hearing about this for the first time, and the commander couldn't have known either.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Just for the sake of completeness, I'd like the witness to see page 220 of the same exhibit. Again, so far as you were aware, did the commander at the time you were in Krajina have any knowledge of excavations going on at the Branjevo state farm?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. He had no knowledge at all, if this is an image of Branjevo. Yes, actually I recognise this picture, but only because I am a surveyor by training and I worked there before the war. This is the old farm.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And lastly, page 240 of the same exhibit. This is Orahovac. Did you or the commander have any knowledge of excavations going on at Orahovac between the 7th and the 27th of September?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the same response: No. I can see here that there is the railroad up there in the upper corner, but no, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, you've talked in the course of your evidence about two operations that you and the commander took part in in July, August and September of 1995. But it was a common occurrence, wasn't it, for either the commander or the Chief of Staff to go on operations outside the Zvornik area?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And when either of them returned, was there any formality to their greeting of one another?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can recall, and this is not something that I'm likely to forget because we were all on good, friendly terms, there were no military formal greetings or giving reports. What would usually happen would be we would come across each other and we would then just say, "Hello," if -- provided we survived. So these were just the usual kind of encounters.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: I mean, to get straight at the point, did you ever see Major Dragan Obrenovic salute Vinko Pandurevic upon his return to the unit and give him a report on the situation there and then?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not that I remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Now, I want to show you a few photographs now, if I may. Can we see 7D581?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: If you could check the number again?

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: I am doing, Judge Kwon, and I'm assured I'm right but I've been assured I'm right many times and have been wrong. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: You recognise that photograph, do you?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Our former command.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And if we can take a walk through it, if we go to 7D582, no, 7D586 first, please. And turn that one round, please. Is that a photograph going through the doors of the command and showing just on the right there the stairway up to the first floor?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. We see the front door, the stairway. To the right of the front door there was a small room where an officer -- a soldier, that is, was on duty.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And what other personnel would have been present when this building was used as command on the ground floor?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were offices to the left, offices of the military police company, and somewhere there my staff office was there, I think if you go straight ahead. To the right there was a room in which we held training sometimes. A medical corps office. And to the left, next to the military police company room, was a passage leading to the canteen.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And was this entrance area frequently busy with people coming in and out and occupying nearby offices?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Usually, yes. I forgot also there was a room where the assistant Chief of Staff for organisation and mobilisation was sitting. So the place was never empty.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Can we now go to 7D582? And does that show us the stairway up to the first floor, the first flight, and 7D583 --

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I suppose so. I suppose that is the stairway.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And that, the second --

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is photographed from the upper landing, and the stairway goes on, leading to the floor where the communications company was housed. That is part of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Now, can we have 7D584, please? Does this show the first floor hallway in which most of the brigade officers had their offices?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That's the hallway. And I could tell you which office is which from my recollection.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Well, I'm going to try and quicken that up by putting some questions to you and I don't want to you mark the photograph. But the first doorway on the right was the office of the duty operations officer, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And then came the offices of Sreten Milosevic. There was a meeting room?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And operational office --

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the operations room.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Then your office?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And then the office of Dragan Obrenovic?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He was right next door to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And on the left-hand side, the chief of signals -- no, the chief of engineering, Jokic?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Then the chief of signals, Petrovic?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And then the assistant commander for moral, religious and legal affairs?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, on that side.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Then Drago Nikolic' office?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He was on that side too.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And at the bottom on the left, Vinko Pandurevic?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That was the commander's office.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: A busy corridor?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was always someone there, and on the other side was the staff command, some messengers, parts of the security detail, the police section attached to the command, a coffee bar, and that was all.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Now, could we have, please, on an entirely unrelated matter put into --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We have only got one more minute left.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: I have only got one more question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Go ahead, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Could we have P377 put into e-court, please, at page 177?

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Now, you've told us previously that you were regularly present at brigade morning meetings and debriefings. This is a record of a --

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: -- debriefing on the 23rd of July. Were you present at that debriefing?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: 23rd July, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And was the commander also present?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And the Chief of Staff?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, as usual, everybody was there.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And at that meeting, was there any discussion of prisoners of war or detainees?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I remember well, the commander demanded that part of the prisoners who were held in our detention be evacuated as soon as possible to Batkovici and he demanded that from the corps command. Why they were kept there, I can't remember. But it wasn't our decision. It was their order.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Thank you. And thank you very much, Mr. Dragutinovic. I apologise to you for having taken so long but I hope you'll understand I did so in the interests of my client.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Haynes. I take it that that brings to an end your cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Your Honour, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Dragutinovic, we will continue on Monday morning, and we will be doing our utmost to try and finish. In the meantime between now and then, same advisory as I had for you yesterday. You're not to communicate with anyone on the subject matter of your testimony. Have a nice weekend, everybody.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I understand. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Monday, the 18th day of June, 2007, at 9.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 1.47 p.m.,
